messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: multiple OOMs detected in runtime-prod pool (gpupool-12) across nodes g12-03,g12-07. Auto-restart triggered for 8 containers. Potential cause: paged-attention allocator fragmentation (slow memory creep). Logs: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY` seen on several crashes. link: https://telemetry.redwood/incident/1772501123
Alex G: seeing the same in traces — tailing logs now. latency spike + 5% 503s for /v1/chat and /v1/embeddings. Customers: two PLG apps reported errors.
Priya S: tagging cs-team and customers affected. cs-ops-bot, please open incident update to customers. :loudspeaker:
cs-ops-bot: Customer incident created: INC-2026-0423. Notifying affected tenants (omitted).
Dan R: quick evidence: heap reported as slowly increasing over ~36h on paged allocator stats. Suspect fragmentation rather than single leak.
Maya L: can we force fallback to non-paged allocator on the pool? I remember a runtime flag we can toggle.
Alex G: yes, we have an env override: REDWOOD_PAGED_ALLOCATOR=disabled (hot-reload supported on runtime v2.3+). Will try canary on one node first.
Dan R: before that, useful logs from the allocator:
```
[2026-03-15T09:02:13Z] allocator: paged_stats: total_reserved=45.7GB, total_committed=42.9GB, fragmented=12.4GB, active_kv_cache=8.1GB
[2026-03-15T09:05:01Z] container runtime: OOM killed process pid=27182 model=rwkv-13b seq_len=2048
[2026-03-15T09:07:44Z] CUDA: err=700, free=120MiB, required=256MiB
```
Alex G: switching node g12-03 to non-paged for canary. command: `kubectl set env ds/inference-runtime REDWOOD_PAGED_ALLOCATOR=disabled -n runtime --selector=node=g12-03`
Priya S: tagging @oncall-nginx to start reroute if canary looks good. If non-paged reduces fragmentation we can roll.
infra-bot: deploy started for selector node=g12-03, rollout id r-2026-03-15-09:18.
Maya L: observed immediate drop in per-process RSS on g12-03 after restart (approx -2.4GB). No crashes so far in 7m.
Dan R: good. But note non-paged increases peak alloc overhead for long contexts; we need to mitigate risk to latency. Suggest also reducing max_seq_len and enabling prefix caching to cut mem usage.
Alex G: rolling config to set MAX_SEQ_LEN=1024 and ENABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=true for canary: `kubectl patch ds inference-runtime -n runtime --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"MAX_SEQ_LEN","value":"1024"}}]'` then similar for ENABLE_PREFIX_CACHE.
Priya S: CS wants ETA for customer impact reduction. Maya how long to confirm stability?
Maya L: give me 20m after canary changes to validate. I'll run load replay against canary node.
Alex G: load replay in progress. Quick note: some models allocate scratch buffers during matmul that are sensitive to allocator behavior — fallback may change perf. We'll set traffic weight low.
Dan R: added temporary routing rule: route 10% traffic to canary, 90% to rest. command: `rdctl route update runtime-prod --canary-weight 10`
infra-bot: routing change accepted.
(20m later)
Maya L: canary stable for 22m. No new OOMs, CPU and P50/P95 latency slightly up (+8ms/+35ms) but within SLA. Fragmentation metrics on canary show fragmented down to 3.2GB from 12.4GB.
Alex G: good signal. Plan: roll non-paged allocator across gpupool-12 in 3 waves to limit perf impact. Wave size 3 nodes. Wave pause 10m + validation.
Priya S: CS update posted: initial mitigation shows canary stable, routing adjusted, customers notified.
Dan R: long-term: we should add allocator compaction and a periodic defrag job. Filing follow-up issue. Also audit models that force large transient allocations and consider tuning matmul workspace.
Alex G: created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4892 "Paged allocator fragmentation -> compaction path and telemetry improvements"
Maya L: added temporary alert rule: if fragmented > 8GB for pool gpupool-*, page an oncall. Rule id: alert-alloc-frag-1772.
Priya S: handoff summary for next oncall:
- Incident: slow-memory creep in paged-attention allocator caused OOMs and container restarts across gpupool-12.
- Mitigation: canaryed REDWOOD_PAGED_ALLOCATOR=disabled on node g12-03, set MAX_SEQ_LEN=1024, ENABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=true, limited canary weight to 10% then rolled in waves.
- Current status: wave 2/3 complete, no new OOMs on rolled nodes; overall fragmentation metrics improving; latency impact measured and within SLA so far.
- Customer impact: transient 503s at peak, two PLG customers saw errors briefly. CS notified and follow-ups in INC-2026-0423.
- Next actions: 1) finish roll after oncall validation, 2) deploy defrag job + compaction work in runtime (issue #4892), 3) run postmortem, include model workspace audit.
Alex G: handing off to night oncall @Dan R for follow-up. Dan, please watch fragmentations and ensure final wave completes.
Dan R: acknowledged — will monitor through 04:00 UTC. If fragmentation regrows >6GB trigger rollback plan (REDWOOD_PAGED_ALLOCATOR=auto-fallback) and notify SRE lead.
infra-bot: incident marked as mitigated for immediate impact. Ongoing follow-ups tracked in GH issue and INC-2026-0423.
Priya S: thanks team. I'll schedule postmortem tomorrow. :coffee:
Maya L: dropping some quick commands for next oncall:
```
# view allocator stats
rdctl metrics query "allocator.paged_stats{pool=\"gpupool-12\"}" --last 1h
# force quick compaction (temporary tool)
kubectl exec -n runtime ds/inference-runtime --selector=node=g12-07 -- /usr/local/bin/alloc_compact --pool gpupool-12
```
Dan R: copy.
Alex G: leaving a short note in runbook with mitigation steps and links.
cs-ops-bot: Post-incident update: customer-facing note queued; will update when postmortem content ready.
Dan R: final: will close handoff once wave 3 completes or if regressions happen will page infra lead.
Maya L: thanks, handing off monitoring to Dan.
